findings.title: A fact records how SURE it is and never how it is KNOWN — the evidence ladder is defined in knowledge/ and never reaches the notebook
findings.expected: A fact carries a derivation label so a corpus count read off forty videos (MEASURED, knowledge/README.md:38) and a vendor statistic arrive at the board as different kinds of claim.
findings.got: facts[] is {id, claim, load_bearing, source, confidence, as_of, note?} and the only evidence-shaped field is confidence: high|medium|low (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:46). The board card types the same three values and nothing else (cards.ts:22). The four-rung ladder governs 'every line in a PATTERNS.md' (knowledge/README.md:34) and is never wired into a notebook fact. The strongest checkable claim in this topic and the weakest vendor claim in another are indistinguishable — both 'medium'.
findings.refuter_pass: 1) Methodic or hard topic? Methodic — the ladder exists, the schema simply has no carrier for it. 2) Would competent execution produce it anyway? Partially: a researcher can smuggle derivation into the confidence string, and the reference run does exactly that — notebook.json:43 writes 'medium — price sources vary by a few thousand' into a field cards.ts:22 types as a three-value union. That is the missing field announcing itself, not a workaround that works: the string is unsortable, unrenderable and type-violating. 3) Present somewhere unread? No — grepped; the ladder appears only in knowledge/README.md, TONE.md, ENGINES.md and template docs, never in pipeline/ or app/_phases/. 4) lens or content? content: an optional derivation enum on a fact is the shared mechanism holding this material, not failing to. Explicitly rejects the lens-bar example at SKILL.md:203-205 ('my domain's evidence never reaches MEASURED') — this domain's evidence DOES reach MEASURED.
findings.l2_priority: Run the topic and check whether the produced notebook can express the difference between a corpus count and a reported claim at all, or whether the researcher is forced into free-text in the confidence field as the Bitcoin run was.

findings.title: the-number is both the domain-specific column and DEFAULT_DIMENSION, so a legitimately empty diagnostic column can never report itself empty
findings.expected: A column with no referent in this domain renders as empty-by-construction and distinguishable from empty-by-omission, so its emptyMeans alarm fires only when it should.
findings.got: the-number's purpose is 'What the price actually did, and over what window' (dimensions.ts:26) — no referent for a format-criticism topic. Its emptyMeans is 'No measured baseline — every claim downstream is unanchored' (dimensions.ts:27), which detects an empty column and reports an unanchored argument: this topic's baseline is forty videos and a timeline, MEASURED per knowledge/README.md:38, while the column is empty. Worse, the same id is DEFAULT_DIMENSION (dimensions.ts:62) and every untagged card falls into it (cards.ts:48,55,61) — so the one column whose emptiness is this topic's diagnosis is guaranteed to render populated with mis-filed cards. The Dimension interface (dimensions.ts:16-23) has no not-applicable affordance and exactly one unconditional emptyMeans string per column.
findings.refuter_pass: 1) Is this just G-000? No, and the distinction is load-bearing. G-000 (accepted-gaps.md:49-57) is 'untagged cards are mis-filed into the wrong column'. This is 'a legitimately-empty diagnostic column is structurally prevented from reading empty'. Same line of code, different failure, and only the second one bites a topic where the emptiness IS the signal. Recorded as a new id per instruction to cite rather than re-raise, and the fallback mechanism itself is cited as G-000. 2) Methodic or topic? Methodic — the coupling of default bucket to a domain-specific column is a design choice, not a property of this topic. 3) lens or content? content: untaggedIds() (cards.ts:91-98) already computes the list, so an explicit untagged bucket plus a two-state emptyMeans is a content edit to the existing mechanism.
findings.l2_priority: Produce the notebook and count how many cards land in the-number by fallback. If any do, the empty-column signal is already destroyed at L2 and does not need L3 to demonstrate.

findings.title: Phase 1 instructs the counter-case as retrieval and Phase 6 as construction — contradictory instructions for one mandatory artefact
findings.expected: One consistent instruction for the mandatory steel-man, with the no-literature case named where the reader first meets the requirement.
findings.got: Phase 1's mandatory last row says 'Search explicitly for the strongest argument that nothing unusual is happening' (RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:32), reinforced as 'not optional and the one most often skipped' (:34). For this topic no literature exists — nobody publishes 'the video-essay format is fine' — so a literal reading offers only skipping (forbidden) or manufacturing a weak steel-man (worse, per ENGINES.md:81-96 D-rigged). Phase 6 sixty lines later resolves it constructively: 'Write the strongest case against your own verdict, with evidence, in the words its believers would use' (:87-93), matched by NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:61-65. The fallback exists; it is unreachable at the point of need, and the board's counter-case column inherits the retrieval framing (dimensions.ts:36-37).
findings.refuter_pass: Explicitly checked the orchestrator's fourth hypothesis ('Phase 1's counter-case row is unsatisfiable for topics with no literature — contradict me if the prompt already provides a fallback') rather than confirming it. THE PROMPT DOES PROVIDE A FALLBACK, at Phase 6, and the hypothesis as stated is refuted. What survives is narrower and still real: two phases give opposite verbs for the same required artefact and the reader hits the retrieval one first. Downgraded from 'unsatisfiable' to 'inconsistent', artifact_check set to present-but-missed accordingly, which per rubric.md:112-113 makes it a discoverability finding. Kept at major only because reachability is high — every no-literature topic in the cast passes through this row. Fix is one clause, so content.
findings.l2_priority: Whether a live run reading Phase 1 first actually finds Phase 6, or skips/manufactures. This is exactly L1's charitable-reading blind spot (SKILL.md:103-106) and cannot be settled on paper.

findings.title: The unhinged tier is a motive claim by definition and the falsifier requirement tests epistemics, not exposure — nothing gates naming a living person
findings.expected: For a topic whose subjects are named living peers, the conclusion layer prices what being wrong costs, or at minimum carries an axis on which a naming rule could hang.
findings.got: unhinged is defined as 'A claim about MOTIVE, which is the least verifiable kind of claim there is' (conclusions.ts:32-33). falsifiableBy is REQUIRED (:55) and works — but a falsifier makes a claim checkable, not survivable. The worked example proves the gap: c-reserve-was-the-product (:163-179) is a well-falsified motive claim about a named administration, which is fine when the subject is a government and is a peer's professional integrity when the subject is a working editor. The Conclusion interface (:36-60) has exactly one grading axis — leap, distance from the evidence — and no exposure or naming axis at all. This creator's line is 'criticise the work, never the person'; the tier is built to cross it and the UI marks it with an emoji rather than a gate.
findings.refuter_pass: Checked the orchestrator's third hypothesis rather than assuming it: 'contradict me if the falsifier requirement already constrains unhinged adequately.' It does not, and the reason is precise — the falsifier is an epistemic instrument on an axis (checkability) orthogonal to the one at issue (exposure). Read the worked unhinged conclusion in full to confirm a good falsifier coexists with an unmitigated motive attribution. Also checked accepted-gaps.md:36-45, which by-designs 'conclusions have no sources' and says nothing about exposure — so this is not suppressed. Filed content, against my own interest: SKILL.md:189-197 lists conclusion-policy and exposure-class as CONTENT slots of a lens pack, so a naming rule is content by the skill's own definition. Noted as the one finding I would argue up if the judge finds convergence, on the ground that leap is the only axis in the interface.
findings.l2_priority: Generate conclusions on this topic and read the unhinged one aloud. If it attributes motive to a named living creator with a tidy falsifier attached, the exposure gap is demonstrated rather than argued.

findings.title: Craft rules labelled MEASURED pool an eight-year corpus without stating the window; three of ten sources carry no publication date
findings.expected: A MEASURED craft claim states the period it was counted over, exactly as the-number demands a window of any figure it holds.
findings.got: ENGINES.md declares n=10 across 6 channels (:11) and stamps craft rules MEASURED (:41, :64, :136, :149, :185) without ever stating the corpus window. The teardowns show it spans polymatter--apple-money.md:6 published 2018-02-23 to economics-explained--north-korea.md:6 published 2026-08-10 — eight years pooled into time-invariant laws. Three of the ten (polymatter--not-target, fireship--big-o-cards, fireship--rubber-duck) carry captured: but no published: field at all. The evidence contract requires MEASURED to carry 'the number, the script that produced it, the sample size' (knowledge/README.md:38) and rules that n is always visible (:45-46) — and never requires the period. For a topic that is about format changing over time, an undated pooled corpus cannot serve as a baseline; if this topic's thesis is right, the engine catalogue is calibrated on a corpus straddling the drift it describes.
findings.refuter_pass: 1) Methodic or topic? Both, and that is why it is worth recording: the defect is general (a measurement with no period) and only a time-sensitive topic notices it. Frequency scored low for that reason, reachability high because every run reads ENGINES.md. 2) Present but missed? Partly — per-source published: frontmatter exists on seven of ten, so the data is recoverable; what is absent is the aggregate window on the claims themselves and any requirement to state it. Scored confirmed-absent against README.md:38's requirement list, with the recoverable half noted. 3) Overclaimed? The stronger version — 'the engines are describing a format mid-drift' — rests on this topic's thesis being right, which is not established. Recorded as motivation in the report, not as the finding. The finding is only that a MEASURED label carries no period. 4) lens or content? content: add period to the evidence contract's MEASURED row and backfill three frontmatters.
findings.l2_priority: n-a — settled on paper. Do not spend L2 budget on it.

findings.title: sources[] is unspecified and renders as bare URLs; no fact-to-source link and no moment-level citation form, though knowledge/README.md:39 already defines one
findings.expected: A citation apparatus that can hold 'video + timestamp' as an atom and connect a fact to the moment that supports it.
findings.got: NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:88 is the entire specification of the field — a heading, no shape, no keys. The reference run resolves the ambiguity as a flat array of bare URL strings (notebook.json:413-428) with no id and no fact-to-source link, so sources[] is a bibliography rather than a citation apparatus. facts[].source is free text (:42, e.g. notebook.json:26), so 'Channel X — Title [4:12]' does fit and does reach the board (cards.ts:24) — the citation survives, degraded. What is lost is the moment: forty facts citing eight videos collapse to eight URLs. knowledge/README.md:39 already specifies the correct form for exactly this evidence ('source · [mm:ss]' + the quoted line) and :47-48 requires the quoted line be present; the notebook schema adopts neither.
findings.refuter_pass: 1) Is the missing thing present elsewhere? The FORM is — knowledge/README.md:39 — but in a document governing PATTERNS.md, not the notebook, so confirmed-absent from the schema with the donor named. 2) Would competent execution produce it anyway? Yes, largely, which is why this is minor and not major: a researcher writes the timestamp into the free-text source field and it renders. The loss is structural (unsearchable, unlinkable, duplicated), not a blocker. 3) This creator's topic being hard? No — every topic citing a moment in a recording (film, game, conflict-OSINT footage) hits it, which is why reachability is med rather than low.
findings.l2_priority: Write the notebook with real timestamped citations and record whether sources[] ended up duplicating the videos or dropping the moments.

findings.title: Phase 5 gives numeric evidence a required craft artefact and structural evidence none, so a numberless notebook passes the row vacuously
findings.expected: A quality-bar row that distinguishes 'this topic has no figures' from 'this topic's figures were made felt', and an equivalent craft obligation for non-numeric evidence.
findings.got: Phase 5 requires 'Every significant figure gets a scale_conversion' (RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:81-86) and the quality bar checks it (:127); CRAFT-BASELINE.md:114-121 gives the craft rationale. For a notebook with no figures the row passes by having nothing, so 'compliant' and 'has no quantitative spine' are indistinguishable on the checklist. Structural evidence — a timestamp, an absence at a moment — gets no counterpart obligation to be made felt, even though the same craft principle applies (an unconverted duration is as inert as an unconverted number). This is non-recognition, not demotion: a deliberate hunt for a rule that privileges MEASURED found none in conclusions.ts (no numeric requirement anywhere), found tension strength keyed to 'checkable' rather than 'measured' (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:39), and found four of five Phase 2 tension shapes non-numeric (:41-49).
findings.refuter_pass: Filed uncertain deliberately. This is the deflated remnant of the charge this seat was dispatched to make — 'a rule privileges MEASURED and demotes my best material'. I looked for that rule in conclusions.ts, RESEARCH-PROMPT.md and NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md and DID NOT FIND IT, and the evidence runs the other way: strength is keyed to checkable, and 4/5 tension shapes are non-numeric. What is left is a vacuously-passed checklist row, which is arguably by-design (a checklist row for a thing you do not have SHOULD pass) and arguably a real asymmetry in craft obligation. Recorded at minor/uncertain rather than dressed up, per rubric.md:107 (default to refuted or uncertain unless the artifact evidence holds).
findings.l2_priority: Run the quality bar against a produced numberless notebook and see whether every row passing reads as a green light or as an absence. If it reads green, upgrade.
